name: Device-side GEMM universal adapter
summary: Expose a kernel-independent host interface that validates arguments, allocates workspace, initializes kernel parameters, and launches a selected GEMM kernel on a CUDA stream.

strategy.intent: Separate device launch orchestration from the internal GEMM kernel implementation.
strategy.mechanism: Translate public arguments into kernel parameters, query workspace requirements, perform capability checks, and launch through a uniform adapter.
strategy.expected_benefit: Makes generated kernels interchangeable behind a stable device-level lifecycle and launch contract.
tradeoffs: Adapter checks and initialization add host-side complexity.
Workspace and hardware capability requirements must remain synchronized with the kernel type.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: Kernel-specific problem, tensor, stride, and scheduler arguments.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Bytes of temporary device storage required by the selected kernel.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: CUDA stream used for initialization and kernel execution.

constraints.expression: Kernel exposes Arguments, Params, can_implement, and workspace_size
constraints.rationale: The adapter delegates validation and parameter construction to a uniform kernel contract.
Some scheduling modes require temporary device storage.
The adapter must construct valid kernel parameters before launch.

references.evidence: The adapter defines the argument, workspace, initialization, update, and stream-based run lifecycle around a kernel type.
